scientific_justification: Factual: For SwinUNETR Protocol A, test LGG recall increased from 0% (0/12) to 100% (12/12) at tau* = 0.03; for ResNet18 Protocol A, recall rose from 75% (9/12) to 91.7% (11/12) at tau* = 0.22.

claim_text: Threshold optimization improved minority sensitivity while reducing HGG specificity.
scientific_justification: Exact description of ROC operating point trade-off: in SwinUNETR Protocol A, 100% LGG sensitivity was achieved at the cost of dropping HGG specificity from 100% to 77.3%.

claim_text: The default threshold of 0.50 is suboptimal for all models.
scientific_justification: Suboptimal specifically for minority sensitivity under severe imbalance, but 0.50 maximizes overall accuracy and HGG specificity for unweighted CNNs.

claim_text: Threshold optimization solves the minority-class problem.
scientific_justification: Overstated: threshold tuning does not improve the underlying latent feature representations (ROC-AUC remains identical) and forces a trade-off against majority false positives.

claim_text: Some models contain useful discriminative information that is not fully reflected by the default 0.50 operating point.
scientific_justification: Supported by high ROC-AUC (e.g. SwinUNETR Prot A AUC = 0.9337) coexisting with 0% sensitivity at tau = 0.50, fully recoverable by operating point calibration.

claim_text: Poor LGG Recall is purely a threshold problem.
scientific_justification: Both representation loss dynamics (class weighting) and operating point thresholds dictate end-to-end performance; threshold shifts cannot fix low AUC.

claim_text: Threshold optimization demonstrates better clinical performance.
scientific_justification: Clinical utility depends on the cost-ratio of false positives vs false negatives; threshold optimization shifts the operating point along the ROC curve rather than proving absolute superiority.

claim_text: Threshold selection should be considered an operating-point sensitivity analysis rather than proof of improved model representation.
scientific_justification: Methodologically rigorous: ROC-AUC is invariant to threshold choice; thresholding calibrates hard decisions on a fixed latent representation.
